content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot post-peak sentiment (e.g., +0.70 sentiment → forecast spikes, then true settles lower).
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.50 to -0.70 → forecast too high, true drops sharply).
- Mean-reversion bias: model holds high forecasts for 5+ days after a spike, but true price often reverts within 7–10 days.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was positive 3–5 days prior, model overreacts; if negative, underreacts — adjust forecast by 5–10% downward if sentiment was negative in last 3 days.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate by 3–8% in early cycles; reduce forecast by 3–5% for first 10 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Spike correction: if model forecasts > +10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 15–20% unless sentiment is strongly bullish (e.g., +0.70 or higher).
